answer.diagnosis: Nearly every structured first-layer unit has very large weights (about ±50 to ±98) on a small 3x3 patch at image rows 1-3, columns 1-3 in the top-left corner. This is far from the central blob, and the surrounding pixels have only small noise-level weights. Units 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 10, 18, 20 and 29 weight the patch strongly positive. Units 5, 6, 9, 14, 15, 21, 24, 27 and 30 weight it strongly negative. Those same units also carry the genuine centre/ring size detectors, so the corner patch feeds the output through the same pathways as the size signal. The patch is therefore a spurious marker: a bright corner square whose presence was correlated with the label during training. The fix is to zero the first-layer weights on that patch for all units. This leaves the centre and ring templates that measure blob size intact.
